text.arabic_uthmani: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا وَمِثْلَهُۥ مَعَهُۥ لِيَفْتَدُوا۟ بِهِۦ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ مَا تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ

words.gloss_range: emphatic opening particle that asserts the whole impossible-ransom verdict as settled report
words.prose: {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) opens with assertion before the ayah stages any hypothetical. The long impossible possession scene is therefore nested inside a verdict already being stated, not a possibility still under negotiation. Its echo with {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) makes certainty and supposition sound related while the grammar keeps them opposed, and the nasal thread keeps the deniers in view through the delayed refusal.

topics.headline: outer assertion frames the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ransom scenario is contained inside an already asserted judgment.
topics.reason: The particle governs the main emphatic statement and the conditional material sits inside that statement.

topics.headline: assertion echoes embedded supposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the similar particles bind the sentence while distinguishing asserted verdict from unreal premise.
topics.reason: The outer particle asserts the judgment, while the later embedded particle introduces the content of the counterfactual premise.

words.gloss_range: definite plural relative pronoun that turns the following denial verb into the subject identity
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not name a group with a bare label; it makes the following clause define the class. The whole ayah is predicated of people identified by {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}), so the impossible wealth and rejected ransom belong to a deed-defined category. Because the phrase is a familiar Quranic formula, the scene reads as a verdict type, not an isolated case.

topics.headline: relative clause defines the subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial is grammatically built into the identity of the group under judgment.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is governed by the opening particle and requires the following clause as its definition.

topics.headline: recognized denial formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase as a recurring verdict-bearing class formula across Quranic usage.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows support a recognized formula without changing the local syntactic role.

words.gloss_range: objectless perfect active denial, covering, or ingratitude presented as a settled collective state
words.root_gloss_range: covering, denial, concealment, and ingratitude, with expiatory covering explicitly not selected by the local Form I verb
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) completes the opening subject with a perfect active verb and no stated object. That makes the denial comprehensive and settled rather than limited to one rejected item, while the plural suffix keeps it collective. The root image of covering and ingratitude remains live, but the local Form I is culpable denial, not expiatory repair; this is why the later self-ransom cannot become a valid covering for what has been covered over. Its clipped sound makes the covering action feel compact and closed before the ayah opens the impossible financial scenario. The word also opens the ayah's movement toward the ransom-futility pattern echoed in 3:91 and toward the escape pressure that continues in 5:37.

topics.headline: objectless settled denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices denial as a settled state of the group, not a single object-specific rejection.
topics.reason: The verb is perfect active and the bundle notes no explicit object.

topics.headline: covering field without expiatory repair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root field of covering while seeing that the selected form marks culpable denial rather than atonement.
topics.reason: The root family includes expiatory forms, but the local surface is Form I denial, so the expiation branch is contrastive only.

topics.headline: denial heads the ransom-futility network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening denial is already tied to punishment, nonacceptance, and the 3:91 ransom-futility pattern.
topics.reason: The contextual rows link this root locally and cross-passage to punishment and nonaccepted ransom.

topics.headline: reported deniers continue into escape pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from addressed believers to reported deniers and the forward movement toward 5:37.
topics.reason: The rows coherently relate the class shift and the next ayah without overriding the local word sense.

topics.headline: compact covering sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a clipped audible closure matching the semantic image of covering before the ayah opens the financial scenario.
topics.reason: The sound row is local to the surface and supports the word-level texture.

words.gloss_range: counterfactual particle that marks the following possession premise as unreal or impossible
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) turns the possession scene into an impossible supposition from its first particle. The ayah can then let all earthly contents and their duplicate accumulate without suggesting a realistic option. Its long protasis delays the short rejection, so the reader feels the maximum offer swell before {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) {{ar:تُقُبِّلَ}} ({{tr:tuqubbila}}) collapses it.

topics.headline: counterfactual impossibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the imagined possession is staged as unreal before it is rejected.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the unreal protasis and controls the following possession scenario.

topics.headline: long protasis before short refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse stretching the imagined offer before delivering a compressed refusal.
topics.reason: The conditional protasis runs from this particle through the Day phrase before the apodosis arrives.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle that embeds the possession content inside the counterfactual frame
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) makes the possession clause grammatically embedded under {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}). The wealth premise is therefore not asserted; it is the content of an unreal supposition. Its resemblance to {{ar:إِنَّ}} ({{tr:inna}}) is productive: certainty and supposition share a sound shape while syntax separates the settled verdict from the imagined premise.

topics.headline: possession subordinated to the counterfactual
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that their possession is never granted as reality, only embedded as hypothetical content.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the content clause inside the counterfactual protasis.

topics.headline: matching particles with opposite force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the matching particle shape bind two levels of the sentence while keeping their force distinct.
topics.reason: The outer particle asserts the verdict and this particle embeds only the unreal possession premise.

words.gloss_range: fronted possessive lām that assigns the imagined earthly totality to the deniers inside the unreal premise
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) begins the fronted possession phrase before the possessed object is named. The grammar first places the imagined ownership on them, then lets the object expand into all that is in the earth. This first possession marker prepares the later reversal in {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}): what is actually for them is not the earth's totality but punishment.

topics.headline: fronted imagined possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the would-be possessors before the enormous object of possession arrives.
topics.reason: The prepositional predicate precedes the relative possession content inside the unreal clause.

topics.headline: opening possession later inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first possession phrase setting up a bookend that closes with assigned punishment.
topics.reason: The same possessive phrase recurs near the end with a reversed object.

words.gloss_range: third-person plural pronoun that fixes the hypothetical possession to the denier group
words.prose: {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) routes the impossible wealth back to the same deed-defined group. The pronoun keeps the ayah in reported verdict mode rather than direct address, and its repeated ending in later forms binds possession, rejected source, and final assignment to the same people.

topics.headline: pronoun tracks the deniers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the whole impossible scenario remains attached to the opening denier class.
topics.reason: The pronoun refers back to the relative group and recurs in later possessive and source phrases.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun opening the unrestricted object: whatever lies within the earth-domain
words.prose: {{ar:مَّا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the possessed object as unrestricted within the earthly domain. With {{ar:جَمِيعًۭا}} ({{tr:jamīʿan}}) it becomes total possession, not a selection from the earth. Its later surface twin, {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}), is re-read as negation, so the same sound first gathers everything and then cancels acceptance.

topics.headline: whatever is in the earth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the imagined possession as comprehensive within the earth-domain, not merely abundant.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun takes the following prepositional phrase as its domain and is intensified by the totality marker.

topics.headline: same surface expands then cancels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local wordplay in which one form opens totality and the later matching form negates acceptance.
topics.reason: The first surface is relative and the second is negative, creating a supported parse-shift effect.

words.gloss_range: locative preposition that makes earth the containing domain of the total possession
words.prose: {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) turns the earth into a container for the imagined total. The scope is maximal within that container, but still bounded as an earthly domain. That matters for the ransom logic: even everything contained within earth cannot reach the scale of the punishment from which they seek separation.

topics.headline: earth as bounded container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ransom reaches the ceiling of earthly containment but remains a bounded domain.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the earth noun and defines the domain for the relative possession phrase.

words.gloss_range: definite singular earth as the recognized material domain and container of imagined ransom value
words.root_gloss_range: land, ground, territory, and the low material domain; locally narrowed to the earth as total ransom-domain
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَرْضِ}} ({{tr:al-arḍi}}) names the recognized earth-domain, not a patch of land. Its singular definite form lets scattered resources be treated as one world-sized material object, governed by {{ar:فِى}} ({{tr:fī}}) and intensified by {{ar:جَمِيعًۭا}} ({{tr:jamīʿan}}). The grounded image also contrasts with {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmati}}), so low material totality cannot answer the rising or standing Day. The 3:91 gold-fill ransom contrast and same-surah scope echoes (5:17; 5:32) sharpen the scale: sovereignty-sized earth becomes a failed human offer.

topics.headline: earth as material ceiling
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the imagined payment reaches the full known material domain.
topics.reason: The definite singular concrete noun is the domain completed by the relative and totality wording.

topics.headline: genitive governed container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that earth is grammatically the container of the possessed total, not merely scenery.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the locative preposition.

topics.headline: grounded domain against standing day
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grounded material image contrasted with the later rising or standing event, while the local sense remains earth-domain.
topics.reason: The root image supports low-ground pressure, but the local phrase selects earth as the domain of possession.

topics.headline: earth totality echoes wider scale texts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local earth-totality as part of a wider scale register, including the 3:91 ransom contrast and same-surah sovereignty scope.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give concrete parallels that intensify, but do not replace, the local ransom-domain role.

words.gloss_range: accusative circumstantial totality marker: altogether, entirely, as a completed collected whole
words.root_gloss_range: gathering scattered parts into a whole; locally the completed totality state, not the process of gathering
words.prose: {{ar:جَمِيعًۭا}} ({{tr:jamīʿan}}) makes the earth-domain possessable as a completed whole. It gathers scattered resources into one ransom mass, then {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) and {{ar:مِثْلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:mithlahu}}) immediately raise the ceiling again. The word also carries a totality formula known from 2:29 and same-surah absolute-scale moments (5:32; 5:48), but here divine gift or scale is redirected into ransom futility. Against the prior call to seek a means (5:35), this gathered stock cannot open escape.

topics.headline: all together as state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the possessed domain is presented as exhaustively complete, not partial.
topics.reason: The accusative adverbial modifies the preceding possession phrase as a state of totality.

topics.headline: scattered resources gathered into one offer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the image of all resources collected into a single offer, while local grammar marks completed totality rather than an act of gathering.
topics.reason: The root image survives as pressure, but the local form names the completed total state.

topics.headline: recurring absolute-scale formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a familiar totality formula redirected into the failed-ransom scene.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give 2:29 and same-surah totality parallels that fit the local phrase.

topics.headline: first maximum before the duplicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that all-earth is not the endpoint; it becomes the base for a second equal amount.
topics.reason: The next coordinated phrase adds an equivalent immediately after the totality marker.

topics.headline: gathered stock versus opened path
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the gathered material mass contrasted with the prior call toward a path-opening means.
topics.reason: The sound and boundary rows coherently frame totality as accumulated stock that cannot open escape.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that adds a second impossible quantity to the total earth phrase
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) refuses to let all-earth stand as the final ceiling. It coordinates {{ar:مِثْلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:mithlahu}}) with the preceding totality phrase, so the imagined possession escalates by addition. The tiny connective makes the doubled ransom arrive without a new clause, fusing totality to its duplicate.

topics.headline: and adds the equivalent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse increasing the impossible offer beyond total earth by coordination.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the equivalent noun with the previous possession object.

words.gloss_range: accusative equivalent with suffix: its exact like, bound to the whole preceding earth-totality
words.root_gloss_range: likeness, equivalence, example, and representation; locally narrowed to exact matching equivalence
words.prose: {{ar:مِثْلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:mithlahu}}) adds not vague extra wealth but the exact counterpart of everything just gathered. Its suffix points back to the whole earth-totality, so the duplicate is dependent on that first maximum. The singular equivalent compresses a doubled universe into one measurable ransom unit, and the 3:91 gold-fill pattern is escalated from precious substance to universal duplication.

topics.headline: duplicate locked to the first totality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second amount has no independent identity; it is the exact counterpart of the first totality.
topics.reason: The attached suffix refers back to the total earth-domain and is later echoed in the instrument pronoun.

topics.headline: equivalent joins the same possessed object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the duplicate as part of the same impossible possession, not an aside.
topics.reason: The accusative coordinated noun belongs to the same possession content.

topics.headline: exact doubling still fails
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even exact duplication of total earth remains insufficient as ransom.
topics.reason: The local sense selects equivalence, and the following apodosis rejects the whole doubled offer.

topics.headline: comparison field narrowed to accounting equivalence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the broader likeness field narrowed into exact ransom accounting, with 3:91 intensified from gold-fill to universal double.
topics.reason: The m-th-l field includes examples and representations, but the suffix-bound local noun selects equivalent amount.

words.gloss_range: adverbial accompaniment phrase making the duplicate present together with the first totality
words.prose: {{ar:مَعَهُۥ}} ({{tr:maʿahu}}) closes the wealth build-up by making the equivalent accompany the first totality at once. The duplicated amount is not sequentially imagined or conditionally added later; it is present with the original as ready ransom stock. The repeated suffix sound in {{ar:مِثْلَهُۥ}} ({{tr:mithlahu}}) and {{ar:مَعَهُۥ}} ({{tr:maʿahu}}) couples the two quantities before the purpose clause turns them into attempted payment.

topics.headline: duplicate present with the original
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both world-sized amounts are imagined as available together.
topics.reason: The adverb of accompaniment relates the equivalent to the original totality as present with it.

topics.headline: wealth phrase sealed by suffix echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the coupled suffixes sealing the doubled-possession phrase before the ransom purpose begins.
topics.reason: The attached pronoun points back to the original totality and the phrase ends the wealth build-up.

words.gloss_range: purpose lām that funnels the impossible possession into the intended act of self-ransom
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) pivots from quantity to purpose. Everything accumulated before it is now grammatically directed toward {{ar:يَفْتَدُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaftadū}}), the attempted self-ransom. In the boundary with 5:35, this reverses the logic of means: instead of seeking a means toward God, the deniers imagine a material means away from punishment.

topics.headline: wealth becomes directed purpose
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vast possession is not decorative excess; it is all funneled into one intended transaction.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following subjunctive verb as a purpose clause.

topics.headline: means toward God reversed into escape payment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prior call to seek a means inverted into an attempted material means of separation.
topics.reason: The boundary row links the purpose particle to the previous ayah without changing the local syntax.

words.gloss_range: Form VIII subjunctive self-ransom verb: they would try to ransom themselves with the amassed wealth
words.root_gloss_range: ransom, redemption, exchange-price, and release; locally the reflexive or middle self-ransom attempt is selected
words.prose: {{ar:يَفْتَدُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaftadū}}) is the hinge where possession becomes transaction. Governed by {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}), it is intended rather than achieved, and its Form VIII shape makes the deniers both actors and intended beneficiaries: they try to ransom themselves. The verb maps a full failed exchange through {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) and {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), and its rare reflexive form sharpens the 3:91 ransom-futility echo. The next ayah's wish to exit the Fire (5:37) continues the escape pressure after payment has failed.

topics.headline: intended ransom action with full valency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the whole transaction map: intended action, instrument, and escape-source.
topics.reason: The verb is governed by the purpose particle and takes the following instrument and separation phrases.

topics.headline: Form VIII self-redemption attempt
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the transaction as intensely self-directed, not a ransom paid for someone else.
topics.reason: The aligned form is Form VIII and the semantic rows support reflexive or middle self-ransom.

topics.headline: rare Form VIII ransom event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this self-ransom verb as a marked lexical event precisely where ransom is futile.
topics.reason: The supplied distribution rows mark this form as exceptional within the ransom root field.

topics.headline: 3:91 formula and forward escape pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the self-ransom attempt as part of a recognized ransom-futility structure, intensified here and carried forward into 5:37.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly connect the construction to 3:91 and to the next ayah escape scene.

words.gloss_range: instrumental preposition plus pronoun compressing the doubled wealth into the means of attempted ransom
words.prose: {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) turns the amassed wealth into instrument or currency. The referent is grammatically compacted into a singular pronoun even after the phrase has imagined all earth and its equivalent, so the impossible mass becomes one tool of exchange. Its suffix chain carries the same object forward from equivalence and accompaniment into attempted payment, while the boundary contrast with 5:35 reverses a divine-direction suffix into a material instrument.

topics.headline: wealth as ransom instrument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the total possession has changed from owned domain into offered price.
topics.reason: The preposition marks instrumentality for the self-ransom verb.

topics.headline: singular suffix carries the huge object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the doubled wealth tracked as one compressed referent moving toward payment, while the exact scope of the pronoun remains locally broad.
topics.reason: The pronoun may refer to the first totality or the combined offer, but the local function is instrument for the whole attempted ransom.

words.gloss_range: separation preposition marking the punishment as the source-domain from which ransom seeks escape
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the ransom aim directional: not gain, but separation from punishment. In the sequence {{ar:يَفْتَدُوا۟}} ({{tr:yaftadū}}) {{ar:بِهِۦ}} ({{tr:bihi}}) {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), the syntax maps action, instrument, and escape-source before the refusal arrives. The later {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) reuses the same preposition to turn the movement back toward the offerers themselves.

topics.headline: from punishment as escape-source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the attempted payment seeks distance from punishment rather than acquisition of reward.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the punishment noun and marks the source of attempted separation.

topics.headline: from punishment becomes from them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated preposition redirecting attempted escape back onto the agents as rejected source.
topics.reason: The first preposition marks escape-source and the later suffixed form marks rejected source.

words.gloss_range: construct punishment noun, governed by separation and specified through the Day-of-Standing chain
words.root_gloss_range: torment and inflicted suffering, with an older sweetness or fresh-water contrast preserved only as lexical tension
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi}}) names what the ransom tries to move away from. Though formally construct, it becomes specific through {{ar:يَوْمِ}} ({{tr:yawmi}}) {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmati}}), creating one eschatological punishment complex before the apodosis negates acceptance. The root's sweetness-versus-torment tension is narrowed here to torment, and same-surah punishment vocabulary (5:18; 5:33; 5:37; 5:40; 5:118) keeps it inside Surah 5's judgment thread. The repeated root later returns as {{ar:عَذَابٌ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābun}}), shifting from the punishment they would escape to the punishment assigned to them.

topics.headline: construct chain specifies the escape target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the feared object as a defined Day-punishment complex, not generic trouble.
topics.reason: The noun is the head of a construct chain completed by the Day and Standing terms.

topics.headline: sweetness field inverted into torment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root tension adding physical force, while the local context selects torment as the escape target.
topics.reason: The lexical family includes sweetness and torment, but the prepositional escape frame selects punishment.

topics.headline: surah-local judgment vocabulary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the term as part of a denial-to-pain judgment network in this surah.
topics.reason: The supplied co-occurrence and same-surah rows place the word in a local punishment field.

topics.headline: first punishment returns expanded
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first punishment as escape target and the later punishment as the broader assigned outcome.
topics.reason: The same noun returns near the close in an indefinite nominative form.

words.gloss_range: construct day term that temporally anchors the punishment in the known Day of Standing
words.root_gloss_range: day, decisive period, or epoch; locally the formulaic eschatological Day rather than an ordinary calendar day
words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمِ}} ({{tr:yawmi}}) sits between punishment and {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmati}}), deepening the construct chain. It gives the punishment its temporal frame, while its construct form depends on the following term for definition. The range of day as decisive period can remain, but locally the phrase is the recognized judgment formula, so the ransom is tested against an appointed eschatological frame rather than an ordinary date.

topics.headline: Day defines the punishment chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment, time, and standing compressed into one construct object.
topics.reason: The construct noun is genitive in the chain and receives definiteness from the following term.

topics.headline: decisive period not mere date
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the Day as a decisive span or epoch of accountability, while the local formula keeps it eschatological.
topics.reason: The broader range is valid, but the construct with Standing selects the known judgment Day.

topics.headline: recognized Day-of-Standing frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ransom scenario entering a familiar judgment formula where material exchange cannot alter the verdict.
topics.reason: The rows support the recurring y-w-m plus q-w-m formula and its judgment-frame function.

words.gloss_range: definite event noun completing the Day-of-Standing formula before the refusal lands
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, establishment, and people-standing imagery; locally the named eschatological event of standing/accountability
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ}} ({{tr:al-qiyāmati}}) completes the escape-target phrase with the known Standing event. The word is not merely a date label: its q-w-m field lets standing, rising, and public accountability remain visible. That gives a concrete reversal to the opening covering-denial: what was covered meets a day when people stand exposed. Because it is the last word before {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}), the full standing-day consequence is named before acceptance is denied. A same-surah consequence link (5:41) keeps this standing-day punishment within Surah 5's unbeliever-punishment discourse.

topics.headline: definite eschatological event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the punishment chain closing on a recognized named event, not a generic rising.
topics.reason: The definite event noun completes the formulaic construct chain.

topics.headline: covering meets public standing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the physical standing image as a reversal of hidden denial, while the local term remains the Day-of-Standing formula.
topics.reason: The q-w-m root supports standing imagery, and the opening denial rows support the concealment contrast.

topics.headline: same-surah consequence field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this Day-punishment phrase inside a wider same-surah consequence discourse.
topics.reason: The supplied same-surah row links punishment descriptions for unbelievers without changing the local formula.

words.gloss_range: negative particle that supplies the compressed apodosis after the long unreal protasis
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is the first word of the answer after the ayah has built the maximum possession, purpose, instrument, and escape target. Its negation makes the verdict immediate: the ransom is not accepted. The same surface sound that earlier opened everything as {{ar:مَّا}} ({{tr:mā}}) now cancels acceptance, and the two-word answer is shorter than the long hypothetical it collapses.

topics.headline: short answer to long condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the long imagined offer being answered by a compact negation.
topics.reason: The particle is the negative apodosis of the counterfactual condition.

topics.headline: nonacceptance already settled
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the failure is not a low price but categorical incommensurability.
topics.reason: The negation with perfect passive presents the counterfactual refusal as settled and scale-independent.

topics.headline: whatever becomes not accepted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated form turning from total inclusion into total cancellation.
topics.reason: The first form is relative and this form is negative, making the local reparse consequential.

words.gloss_range: Form II perfect passive of evaluative acceptance, negated as the settled refusal of the ransom
words.root_gloss_range: facing, receiving, approving, accepting, and turning toward; locally evaluative acceptance is denied
words.prose: {{ar:تُقُبِّلَ}} ({{tr:tuqubbila}}) supplies the verb that resolves the conditional. In the standard passive, the accepting or rejecting agent is not named, so the offer's nonacceptance stands as an absolute result while {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) keeps the rejected source visible. The q-b-l field makes refusal more than failure to take payment: the offer is not favorably faced, received, or approved. The same-surah echo with accepted offering in 5:27 and the 3:91 ransom-futility formula make this denied acceptance especially sharp. The doubled middle consonant makes the refused reception feel tightened shut under negation, while the active variant exposes agency pressure but does not replace the local passive.

topics.headline: passive perfect nonacceptance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices refusal as a completed verdict, not a negotiable interaction.
topics.reason: The local form is perfect passive in the negated apodosis.

topics.headline: not faced or favorably accepted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices nonacceptance as denied favorable reception, while the local sense remains acceptance rather than physical facing alone.
topics.reason: The root field includes facing and receiving, and Form II supports evaluative acceptance in this passive context.

topics.headline: active variant exposes hidden agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how a variant can surface accepting agency, while the canonical local surface foregrounds the rejected offer.
topics.reason: The variant evidence is valid for contrast, but the aligned local form remains passive.

topics.headline: offering echo and 3:91 formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 5:27 accepted offering reversed into refused ransom and 3:91 not-accepted ransom logic reprised.
topics.reason: The supplied rows give concrete same-surah and cross-passage acceptance parallels.

topics.headline: tightened refusal sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compressed sound of the acceptance verb under negation as a tightened refusal.
topics.reason: The sound row is surface-local and coheres with the negated passive refusal.

words.gloss_range: source phrase marking the rejected offer as coming from the deniers themselves
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) shifts attention from amount to source. The failure is not that the imagined price is too small; the offer is not accepted from them. This also reverses the prepositional movement of {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}): they try to move from punishment, but the refusal points back from them as the source. The suffix then flows directly into {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}), keeping the same group audible as the verse turns to assigned punishment.

topics.headline: from them, not deficient price
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rejection attaching to the persons offering, not to a shortage in the price.
topics.reason: The preposition plus suffix identifies the source from whom the ransom is not accepted.

topics.headline: for them to from them to for them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices possession, rejection, and assignment tied together by a local prepositional arc.
topics.reason: The rows trace the movement from possessive phrase to source phrase and back to possessive phrase.

topics.headline: same group kept in the ear
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the same group carried from rejected source into final assignment.
topics.reason: The suffix echo is local and immediately precedes the closing possession phrase.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a new real-state clause after the failed hypothetical
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does not add another item to the ransom list. It resumes the verdict after the conditional collapse and moves from imagined transaction to declared reality. Joined directly to {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}), it carries nonacceptance into the final assigned possession without a logical pause.

topics.headline: returns from hypothetical to declared state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final clause as a fresh assertion of reality after the unreal offer fails.
topics.reason: The conjunction introduces the coordinated nominal coda rather than continuing the ransom list.

topics.headline: short turn into possession reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the resumption fused to the possessive phrase that assigns the final outcome.
topics.reason: The conjunction attaches directly to the following possessive phrase.

words.gloss_range: fronted possessive phrase assigning punishment to the same denier group as their actual share
words.prose: {{ar:لَهُمْ}} ({{tr:lahum}}) fronts the possessor before the punishment is named. The clause first says the outcome is for them, then reveals that it is {{ar:عَذَابٌ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābun}}). This reverses the earlier hypothetical possession in {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}): what truly belongs to them is not all earth and its duplicate, but punishment after the failed substitute.

topics.headline: possessor first in final clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the punishment assigned to them before the noun itself appears.
topics.reason: The prepositional predicate is fronted before the delayed subject.

topics.headline: imagined wealth becomes actual punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same possession logic inverted from hypothetical wealth to actual punishment.
topics.reason: The opening possessive phrase is echoed at the close with a reversed object.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative punishment noun, delayed after the fronted possessor and broadened beyond the earlier Day construct
words.root_gloss_range: torment, inflicted suffering, and a sweetness contrast in the root family; locally the torment pole is selected
words.prose: {{ar:عَذَابٌ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābun}}) is the delayed subject that reveals what has been assigned to them. Unlike {{ar:عَذَابِ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābi}}), it is indefinite and free of the Day construct, so the final punishment opens beyond the earlier specified escape target. The repeated root turns attempted separation into assignment, not refreshment, and with {{ar:أَلِيمٌۭ}} ({{tr:alīmun}}) it enters a familiar painful-punishment formula. The tanwīn cadence also links the total offer in {{ar:جَمِيعًۭا}} ({{tr:jamīʿan}}) to the open-ended consequence at the close.

topics.headline: final punishment opens beyond the specific target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the second punishment term broadened from specified Day-punishment to open-ended assigned punishment.
topics.reason: The noun is nominative indefinite and no longer bound in the earlier construct chain.

topics.headline: revealed after assignment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause assigning the outcome before naming what the outcome is.
topics.reason: The noun is the delayed subject after the fronted predicate.

topics.headline: root pressure returns as assigned torment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root-family pressure returning at closure, while the local sense remains punishment rather than refreshment.
topics.reason: The sweet-water branch is contrastive only; the context selects the torment pole.

topics.headline: painful-punishment seal begins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the closing noun entering a recognizable painful-punishment formula and echoing the offer-totality cadence.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence rows support the formula, and the sound row connects the indefinite endings locally.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative adjective qualifying punishment as painful, pain-bearing, or pain-inflicting
words.root_gloss_range: pain, hurt, pain-causing and pain-felt force; locally an agreed adjective defining the punishment quality
words.prose: {{ar:أَلِيمٌۭ}} ({{tr:alīmun}}) locks the final quality onto {{ar:عَذَابٌ}} ({{tr:ʿadhābun}}) by agreement. The close is therefore not merely that punishment exists for them, but that the assigned punishment is pain-bearing and felt as agony. The faʿīl pattern allows both pain-causing and pain-experienced force, while the formulaic pairing makes the ending a recognized consequence seal. As the last word, its tanwīn cadence leaves the ayah on the felt quality of the verdict.

topics.headline: pain quality attached to punishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices pain as the specific quality of the punishment, not a floating description.
topics.reason: The adjective agrees with the preceding indefinite nominative noun.

topics.headline: pain-causing and pain-felt force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the punishment as both inflicting and experienced pain, while the local grammar keeps it adjectival qualification.
topics.reason: The faʿīl pattern supports durable pain force without replacing the noun-adjective relation.

topics.headline: recognized painful-punishment formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah closing on a familiar Quranic consequence marker after ransom failure.
topics.reason: The supplied rows identify the formula and same-surah pain thread.

topics.headline: paired indefinite sound seals the close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final adjective sealing grammar, formula, and cadence together.
topics.reason: The tanwīn and final position support the audible closure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The counterfactual construction joins all that is in the earth, its equal alongside it, the purpose clause لِيَفْتَدُوا۟ بِهِۦ, and the passive refusal مَا تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah builds the largest imaginable asset aggregate, doubles it with a counterpart, directs it into substitution for the liable persons, and then blocks the transaction at acceptance. The limit case makes judgment non-commutable rather than merely expensive.

activation_trace.role: Completion without dispersal or lack makes the terrestrial holding an exhaustive rather than merely large tender.
A matching counterpart doubles the exhaustive holding and tests whether equivalence can purchase release.
Giving one thing in place of another supplies the proposed asset-for-person substitution.
Reception with approval is the decisive gate, and the passive negation closes it before price comparison can matter.

changed_reading.before: Even an enormous ransom would be insufficient.
changed_reading.after: The doubled total is a limit test showing that final liability cannot be commuted through asset substitution at all.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: كَفَرُوا۟ names the liable group, while يَفْتَدُوا۟ and مَا تُقُبِّلَ stage an attempted removal of consequence by a substitute.
baseline_models.mechanism: The root network of ك ف ر links concealment of truth with the more distant image of covering an offense through expiation. The liable coverers try to make property perform a second covering operation, but failed acceptance prevents owned wealth from becoming self-authored expiation.

activation_trace.role: Blocking or concealing truth marks the agents whose attempted transaction is refused.
The branch of covering an offense until it is effaced raises the exploratory possibility that the ransom seeks to manufacture expiation.
A paid substitute is the proposed instrument for removing the persons from consequence.
Refusal withholds the approval required for a substitute to acquire expiatory force.

changed_reading.before: Disbelievers unsuccessfully try to buy relief.
changed_reading.after: Those defined by covering cannot turn possession into a second, expiatory covering; acceptance, not ownership, would have to transform the substitute.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: عَذَاب occurs on both sides of the refusal and ends in the qualifier أَلِيم, while the first occurrence is what the ransom seeks escape from.
baseline_models.mechanism: The punishment root carries both severe pain and withholding or preventing. Framed by a failed escape instrument and capped by the causative quality أليم, punishment can be read as a two-layer state: denied release or access that is itself painfully experienced at the Rising.

activation_trace.role: Withholding, prevention, and weaning supply a deprivation layer to both occurrences of punishment.
Severe infliction supplies the direct painful layer rather than reducing punishment to deprivation alone.
Rising and resurrection locate the blocked release at the final standing of creatures.
Causing pain makes the final adjective an explicit confirmation of experienced injury.

changed_reading.before: The ayah threatens generic painful torment.
changed_reading.after: The ayah threatens a final condition in which release is withheld and that blocked condition is actively painful.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The first لَهُم counterfactually assigns all terrestrial contents to them; after refusal, وَلَهُمْ assigns punishment to them.
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated possession construction reverses its object. Hypothetical universal ownership is granted only to be made ineffective, while punishment is the one allotment stated without a counterfactual. The grammar moves from imagined assets held by them to consequence fixed for them.

activation_trace.role: The whole lower terrestrial domain supplies the maximal scope of the counterfactual possession.
Unbroken totality removes any residual asset that might remain outside their imagined ownership.
The repeated severe consequence becomes the enduring object of the final non-counterfactual allotment.

changed_reading.before: They hypothetically own everything but cannot spend enough.
changed_reading.after: The ayah grammatically cancels imagined ownership as effective power and replaces it with the only fixed possession: consequence.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier paired offerings undergo opposite acceptance outcomes, followed by the rule that God accepts only from those who place themselves in protective restraint. That pattern shifts 5:36 from an inadequate-object model to an offerer-conditioned model: the doubled object cannot repair the condition encoded by مِنْهُمْ.

activation_trace.role: Refused reception with approval is the focus result that requires explanation.
Three acceptance forms contrast two offerers and explicitly attach approved reception to the source from whom an offering comes.
Offering for nearness to God supplies the ritual approach whose material similarity does not guarantee equal reception.
Placing oneself in protection supplies the stated qualifying condition for an acceptable giver.

structural_cues: 5:27 and 5:36 repeat passive acceptance language together with a مِن phrase identifying the source.
The accepted and unaccepted offerings in 5:27 precede the escalation from refused offering to violence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies unequal acceptance and an explicit offerer condition; I infer that مِنْهُمْ in 5:36 makes subject-condition override object-size. A live alternative is that the refusal is chiefly due to the late eschatological moment rather than the offerers' prior condition alone.

changed_reading.before: No object is valuable enough to be accepted as ransom.
changed_reading.after: The decisive defect lies in those from whom the object comes; infinite enlargement cannot convert an unqualified giver into an acceptable one.

context_deltas.mechanism: 5:32 uses جَمِيعًا twice to make one killed or preserved life scale as all people, while locating violent excess in the earth. Against that moral totalization, 5:36 gathers all the earth and doubles it as a proposed counterweight. The repeated totality changes the focus from wealth hyperbole into a failed attempt to answer non-arithmetic liability with arithmetic accumulation.

activation_trace.role: Exhaustive totality turns the offered property into a purported complete counterweight.
The terrestrial domain defines the full material side of the proposed balance.
Twice-repeated completeness scales the moral consequence of one life to humanity without remainder.
The same terrestrial field holds both the life-wide offense and the later excess that material totality cannot offset.

structural_cues: 5:32 repeats the one-life/all-people equivalence twice before 5:36 presents all-earth/its-like equivalence.
Both ayat combine totalizing language with the earth, but one totals moral consequence and the other totals property.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies matched totalizers and equivalence constructions; I infer a scalar reversal in which material doubling fails against morally total liability. A live alternative is that the repetition is rhetorical intensification without an intended accounting relation.

changed_reading.before: All earthly wealth plus the same amount is merely the largest imaginable sum.
changed_reading.after: The doubled sum is a deliberately wrong kind of total: arithmetic property cannot balance a context where one life already carries humanity-wide weight.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate lead-in preserves repentance specifically before capture, then commands protective restraint, seeking a means, and effort along a path. The focus follows with a purpose-built ransom that is not accepted at the Rising. The contrast separates a timely lived route from a late object offered as price.

activation_trace.role: Denied approval marks the failure of the late proposed instrument.
Temporal precedence marks a real before-condition under which turning remains consequential.
Putting oneself in protection supplies an enacted present posture rather than a future payment.
A traversable extended path makes deliverance procedural and lived rather than purchasable at the endpoint.

structural_cues: The branchless وَسِيلَة in 5:35 is a sought means embedded between restraint and striving.
The sequence moves from repentance before seizure, to seeking and striving, to a counterfactual offer at the Day of Rising.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit before-condition and a present means/path immediately ahead of the failed ransom; I infer that timing and enacted traversal distinguish valid means from invalid price. A live alternative is that the refusal is categorical for the named group and not primarily a deadline contrast.

changed_reading.before: The ayah says that the available ransom is too late or too small.
changed_reading.after: The ayah opposes two kinds of means: a path entered while action remains possible and a maximal object tendered only after that path has closed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah unfolds the focus punishment spatially: its occupants will exit, are explicitly not exiting, and have punishment that remains in place. This activates the prevention branch of ع ذ ب and turns failed ransom into failure to obtain a transition out of a resident condition.

activation_trace.role: Withholding and prevention make punishment capable of naming blocked release as well as inflicted pain.
Passage to the outside is first desired and then explicitly negated, supplying the blocked transition.
The repeated punishment term binds non-exit to the focus root's withholding image.
Remaining or residing in a place gives the punishment durative spatial stability.

structural_cues: 5:37 uses a desire-to-exit / no-exit reversal and closes with the predicate مُّقِيم.
The failed escape payment in 5:36 is followed immediately by failed physical exit in 5:37.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed ransom followed by negated exit and resident punishment; I infer that the transaction's desired output was a state transition and that refusal locks the state. A live alternative is that 5:37 only elaborates duration, while deprivation remains secondary to pain.

changed_reading.before: The ransom cannot cancel a sentence of pain.
changed_reading.after: The ransom cannot open an exit: punishment is a stable non-exiting residence whose prevention is part of its painful force.

context_deltas.mechanism: 5:40 declares that dominion of the heavens and earth belongs to God and places punishment and forgiveness under divine determination. Read back into 5:36, the hypothetical holders try to tender the complete earth to the sovereign whose domain it already is. The offer fails not only in amount but in alienable title.

activation_trace.role: The full lower terrestrial domain is the object hypothetically placed in the offerers' hands.
Substitution attempts to transfer that domain as the price of the persons' release.
Sovereignty assigns the relevant domain to the judge rather than to the hypothetical tenderers.
The same earth named in the tender is included inside the sovereign's dominion.
Inflicting punishment remains an exercise of sovereign determination, not a claim that the debtor can buy from its owner.

structural_cues: 5:36 counterfactually says they possess all the earth; 5:40 categorically assigns dominion of heavens and earth to God.
5:40 coordinates punishment and forgiveness with divine will immediately after the legal examples of 5:38-39.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies identical terrestrial scope under hypothetical possession and actual sovereignty; I infer a property-rights defect in the tender. A live alternative is that sovereignty signals unrestricted authority without inviting a literal title analysis.

changed_reading.before: They cannot pay enough from what they own.
changed_reading.after: Their maximal tender is structurally void because it offers the sovereign a domain already under the sovereign's title and determination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The judgment pericope moves from consumers of illicit gain to judgment by equity and then forbids exchanging divine signs for a small price. The focus's all-earth-plus-equal offer becomes the limiting case of the same corruption test: replacing a small price with the largest conceivable one still cannot purchase a changed judgment.

activation_trace.role: A substitute offered for release supplies the focus transaction that the judgment sequence tests.
Non-approval prevents the proposed consideration from entering the judgment relation.
Illicit and defective gain supplies the corrupt economic pressure surrounding adjudication.
Repeated adjudication places the illicit-gain problem inside a formal judgment setting governed by equity.
Exchange between sale and purchase identifies the prohibited conversion of revelation into consideration.
Sale-value supplies the small-price pole that the focus expands to a maximal-price test.

structural_cues: 5:42 coordinates illicit gain with the command to judge by equity.
5:44 forbids sale for a small price and ends by naming the non-judging group with the same ك ف ر root as the focus subjects.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies corrupt gain, impartial judgment, and prohibited sale-value; I infer that 5:36 universalizes the anti-bribery principle by testing the maximum possible price. A live alternative is that the ransom image is only eschatological hyperbole and not a back-reference to corrupt adjudication.

changed_reading.before: No ransom is large enough to reverse the outcome.
changed_reading.after: Judgment is categorically nonpurchasable: the difference between a small corrupt price and all the earth doubled is quantitatively vast but legally irrelevant.

context_deltas.mechanism: 5:45 first states exact bodily counter-equivalences, then makes voluntary relinquishment of the retaliation claim a charity and an expiation. That sequence sharpens the focus contrast: doubled external possessions cannot self-produce a covering, whereas releasing a rightful claim can acquire expiatory force.

activation_trace.role: The expiatory covering branch makes the liable group's attempted ransom readable as a failed bid to erase consequence.
Owned property is proposed as an external substitute for the persons under liability.
Matching injury with injury establishes the exact equivalence that a claimant may legitimately demand.
Charitable giving converts relinquishment of that matched claim into a morally directed transfer.
Explicit expiatory covering supplies a context-valid transformation absent from the focus's rejected self-ransom.

structural_cues: 5:45 moves from repeated part-for-part equivalence to voluntary release and then explicitly names كَفَّارَة.
The focus also joins equivalence, substitution, and the ك ف ر root, but its object is retained wealth offered for the offerers themselves.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact retaliation, charitable release, and explicit expiation; I infer that relinquishing a valid claim differs categorically from leveraging possessions for oneself. A live alternative is that the expiation in 5:45 accrues only to the relinquishing claimant, so the contrast should not be turned into a general rule for an offender's pardon.

changed_reading.before: The focus simply denies that wealth can serve as ransom.
changed_reading.after: The context distinguishes failed self-protective substitution from a live expiatory act: not possessing an equivalent, but relinquishing a rightful equivalent, can cover.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus gathers all terrestrial assets around the liable persons as a substitute. 5:48 later gathers all persons in return to God. The repeated جَمِيعًا reverses what is collected: at judgment the agents themselves return together, so their aggregate property cannot stand in for the returning selves.

activation_trace.role: Complete aggregation collects every terrestrial asset on the offer side.
Substitution tries to let the gathered asset mass occupy the liable persons' place.
Return brings the accountable agents themselves back to the source of judgment.
A gathered company makes all persons, rather than all their holdings, the final collective before God.

structural_cues: The same adverb جَمِيعًا modifies all terrestrial contents in 5:36 and the universal human return in 5:48.
Both constructions terminate in judgment language: non-acceptance at the Rising and disclosure of disputed action after return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a repeated totalizer applied first to assets and then to returning agents; I infer an assets-to-agents reversal that defeats substitution. A live alternative is that جَمِيعًا is only a recurrent universal quantifier without a designed contrast.

changed_reading.before: People arrive with an insufficient aggregate of property.
changed_reading.after: The wrong aggregate has been assembled: all property cannot replace the all-together return of the accountable persons themselves.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it cross-activates the literal covering branches of ك ف ر and و ر ي with the imitation branch of م ث ل, while the focus surface most directly denotes unbelief and a quantitative counterpart. It remains anchored in focus words and in 5:31's exact earth/like/cover sequence. Downstream prose should present it only as a material echo, never as the direct lexical gloss of the focus.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: كَفَرُوا۟, all the earth, and وَمِثْلَهُۥ form a cover/counterpart cluster whose strange material potential is activated by the raven episode.

activation_trace.role: Literal covering supplies the exploratory material action latent behind the focus group's defining root.
Following a model reframes the added counterpart as another attempted earthly procedure, not only a numerical equal.
The literal ground supplies the material that receives and hides the exposed consequence.
The human explicitly follows the raven as an executable model for dealing with exposure.
Twice-repeated concealment makes covering with earth the learned response whose moral insufficiency can echo into the focus.

changed_reading.before: A second earth-sized amount is added to a failed financial ransom.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, even duplicating the whole earthly covering procedure cannot bury exposed liability; material concealment scales without becoming moral removal.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because مِثْلَهُ in the focus plainly functions as a counterpart, while the punitive-example branch belongs to the wider م ث ل network. It remains worth carrying because 5:38 explicitly supplies نَكَٰلًا, an exemplary deterrent, next to earned recompense. Downstream prose should qualify it as activated wordplay about becoming an example, not substitute that sense into the focus syntax.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus counterpart root م ث ل and its failed exchange are re-pressured by the immediately following legal language of earned recompense and exemplary punishment.

activation_trace.role: The branch of punitive example supplies a strange alternative pressure on the otherwise quantitative counterpart.
The attempted substitute defines the failed counterprice against the possibility of exemplary consequence.
Acquisition ties legal consequence to what the agents themselves have earned rather than to later replacement assets.
A punishment that deters others activates the exemplary branch and opposes example-making to price-taking.

changed_reading.before: They offer an equal amount as a counterprice for release.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, no counterprice prevents consequence from becoming an example: what was earned remains attached to the agent and instructive to others.

strongest_changes: 5:27 relocates the acceptance problem from the magnitude of the offering to the condition of those from whom it comes.
5:32 turns all-earth arithmetic into a failed answer to life-wide moral totality.
5:34-35 distinguish a timely lived means and path from a maximal late price.
5:37 unfolds punishment as blocked exit and durable residence, not pain alone.
5:40 and 5:42-45 expose three transaction defects: the tendered domain belongs to the sovereign, judgment is nonpurchasable, and expiation arises through relinquishment rather than possession.
5:48 reverses the aggregate from all assets to all accountable agents returning together.
summary.what_was_special: The pericope repeatedly reuses the focus roots and constructions in changed roles: accepted versus rejected offerings, one life equated with all people, before versus final refusal, terrestrial possession versus sovereignty, small price versus doubled total price, exact retaliation versus charitable release, and gathered property versus gathered return. These shifts make the ayah a boundary on substitution rather than a bare claim that the ransom is very large.
remaining_uncertainties: The moral-accounting relation between 5:32 and 5:36 may be deliberate scalar reversal or only rhetorical recurrence.
The property-title and anti-bribery readings depend on reader-supplied transactional arrows even though their packet cues are close.
In 5:45 the beneficiary of expiation may be the claimant who relinquishes retaliation, so that delta should not be generalized into an offender-pardon formula.
The two outliers depend on distant root branches and should remain qualified echoes rather than direct glosses.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Infinite-seeming substitution cannot create acceptance.** `ف د ي B001` is putting up a ransom/substitute, `ج م ع B009` wholeness without loss, and `ق ب ل B004` receiving with acceptance. Even a doubled whole earth remains unreceived. I infer that no quantitative substitute can replace the missing relational condition of acceptable approach established in 5:27.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Accumulated possession cannot become an accepted substitute.** Fixed **ف د ي / B001** (“putting something up as ransom or substitute”) supplies the attempted exchange, while fixed **ق ب ل / B004** (“receiving with acceptance”) is negated. The preceding 5:35 locates approach in striving, and 5:37 denies escape even after the ransom fails. I infer that doubling the quantity cannot repair a categorical mismatch between owned earth and accountable action. The scenario reads as failure of substitutability, not insufficiency of price.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:37’s denied exit and 5:39’s accepted repair confirmed that the problem is categorical substitutability, not an earthly ransom whose amount was too small.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi örtme ve görünmez kılma çekirdeğini; zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme, külün toprakla kapanması ve yıldızların güneş ışığında görünmemesi gibi gerçekleşmelerle açıkça destekler.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın örtme çekirdeğini korur; zırh, silah, kül ve gök cisimleriyle ilgili kullanımlar bu çekirdeğin yapıya bağlı gerçekleşmeleri olarak ayrılır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka bir şeyle örterek görünmesini engellemek veya kapalı duruma getirmektir. Zırhın giysiyle, kişinin silahla ya da külün savrulan toprakla örtülmesi bu işlemin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin üstünü kapatarak onu görünmez veya örtülü duruma getirme işlemi.
Zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme ve külün üstünün toprakla kapanması çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
Güneşin yıldızları görünmez kılması da görsel örtme sonucu üzerinden bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar örtme ve kapatma çekirdeğinde birleşir; farklı örnekler bu işlemin nesne, giysi, silah, kül ve gök görünümü üzerindeki gerçekleşmelerini gösterir.
